title: Adversarial structured-output recovery benchmark for JSON-mode with streaming and toolcall interference
creator: Anika Rao
description: Create an end-to-end benchmark and test harness that intentionally exercises adversarial/edge-case failures in JSON mode when responses are streamed and when interleaved tool/function calls occur. Goal is to characterize failure modes, quantify recovery success rates, and produce mitigation patches (decoder gating heuristics, reassembly strategies, and fallback policies). This ticket captures test design, implementation plan, expected artifacts, and acceptance criteria.
background_and_motivation: We continue to see intermittent production regressions where partial streamed payloads or toolcall tokens corrupt structured outputs, leading to downstream parsing failures. Existing fuzz suites cover many token-level corruptions but do not simulate real-world operational interference: chunk boundary splits inside JSON tokens, tool call tokens injected mid-object, KV-cache warm/cold transitions, and model fallback switches mid-stream. This benchmark will bridge that gap and produce deterministic failure repros for fixes and regression prevention.
acceptance_criteria: A reproducible benchmark harness that can run 1k synthetic scenarios and report pass/fail and failure taxonomy for each run.
Clear taxonomy of failure modes (e.g., broken tokens at chunk boundary, truncated arrays, interleaved toolcall artifacts, partial closing braces) with example payloads stored as artifacts.

Automated remediation experiments: at least two mitigation strategies implemented and measured (e.g., chunk-aware reassembly + strict constrained-decoder backoff; streaming sentinel insertion + schema-aware stitcher) with quantitative improvement >= 80% on targeted failure cases relative to baseline.
Test outputs integrated into CI gating (smoke subset) and an operator playbook outlining rollforward/rollback steps for runtime changes.
Dashboard card in runtime-1.22 release showing benchmark pass-rate, worst-case latency delta, and cost impact for mitigation strategies.
Documentation describing test harness, how to add new scenarios, and how to reproduce local failures (README in repo).
test_plan: Harness: extend existing 'structured-output-stability-playground' runner to add adversarial scenario generator and deterministic seeds.

Scenario types: chunk-split (break JSON tokens across N stream frames), toolcall-splice (inject tool invocation tokens within JSON structures), kv-warm-cold (simulate cached vs cold KV behaviors mid-request), fallback-swap (switch model variant mid-stream), and noise-insertion (random token insertions near structural delimiters).
Metrics: pass/fail, time-to-first-valid-parse, recovery-latency (ms), token-overhead, and successful-schema-assertions (%).
Environments: run against hosted-runtime (staging), dedicated pool (dev reserved GPUs), and private docker image for on-prem parity. Use the same model family across runs to isolate decoder behavior.
Mutation matrix: vary sequence lengths (short/medium/long), temperature/decoder settings, and streaming chunk sizes to exercise kernel selection changes.
Golden prompts: 25 real-customer-like prompts derived from internal incident logs (anonymized), plus 75 synthetic cases covering combinatorial edgecases.
implementation_steps: Design adversarial scenario DSL and generator (lib/adversary) to emit deterministic token-level streams.
Add a streaming reassembly shim that can be toggled on/off in the runtime harness to simulate pre/post-fix behavior.

Implement two mitigation prototypes in the runtime harness: (1) schema-aware stitcher that buffers until top-level object closure heuristics, (2) constrained-decoder backoff that lowers sampling entropy near structural tokens and triggers automatic resend of last chunk when corruption detected.
Integrate benchmark runner with CI and create a smoke test that runs a minimal subset on every PR touching streaming or structured-output code paths.
Store failing scenario artifacts in S3 and link them from the ticket for triage and postmortem use.
Create dashboard card and alert rule in Console for benchmark degradation across nightly runs.
Write operator playbook for deployment of mitigation with A/B rollout and immediate rollback criteria.
dev_notes: Tradeoffs: Buffering until object closure improves correctness but increases tail latency; constrained-decoder backoff changes sampling dynamics and could degrade creative non-JSON workloads—we will gate by request route and content-type headers.
Prioritization: focus on routes serving JSON-mode and tool-enabled chat first to limit surface area.
Instrumentation: add additional telem events for streaming-chunk-boundary, reassembly-retries, and toolcall-interleaved-detected to help classify failures in production.
Compatibility: ensure prototypes are no-ops for runtime configurations that don't enable JSON-mode or streaming to avoid cross-impact.
Open question: whether to implement stitcher in the gateway (pre-runtime) vs inside the runtime — initial prototype in gateway shim for faster iteration.
review_comments: PM (Sara Velasquez): Please ensure the baseline includes current prod decoder settings so we can quantify real-world improvement.
Design (Liam O'Connor): Add example UI snippets for how Console will surface 'in-flight parse failures' and suggested remediation steps for customers.
SRE (Priya Nambiar): We need a clear rollback plan with metrics thresholds — add in dev_notes and operator playbook.

qa_notes_and_next_steps: Run initial 1k-scenario sweep in staging by 2026-03-12 and capture baseline failure taxonomy.
If mitigation prototypes show >80% improvement on targeted classes, schedule runtime patch review and canary rollout to dedicated pool for runtime-1.22.
Assign follow-up tickets for any lingering failure subtypes with ownership and target fixes.
